cardio: 12 min zone 2 run to the gym + 12 min zone 2 run back. Arrilaga.
notes: **The squat depth-limiter test ran and it answered decisively: ankle and brace, not hip range.** Heels elevated opened depth "way open"; hugging the plate made it "way easier"; and going wider was actively WORSE — "almost like sumo squats these are actually harder," with the inner thighs becoming the limiter. That last one contradicts the untested 2026-08-26 assumption that wider helps. Baseline also showed the pelvic tuck he was asked to look for. Alongside the test, two milestones: **45/side now touches the pin-14 support bars with a 3s pause — a month ago that was bodyweight-only** — and his own read on 80/side, *"feels similar to what 45/s felt when we first started this program."* Leg press hit knees-to-chest on every set including the first.

exercises.notes:
**THE DEPTH-LIMITER TEST — result: ankle + brace.** Stance context in his words: *"toes in v."*
- **1. Baseline:** *"heel flexibility in ankles and inner hips the limiter — definitely a hip tuck here."* Both the ankle and the adductors named, and the pelvic tuck confirmed.
- **2. Plate under each heel:** *"depth way open on this, ankle not limiter at all."* Removing the dorsiflexion demand removes the ceiling. **Ankle confirmed as a major limiter.**
- **3. Wider + more toe-out:** *"almost like sumo squats, these are actually harder — inner thighs are limiter."* **Negative result, and a useful one:** widening does not buy depth, it trades the ankle for the adductors.
- **4. Hugging the 45 at the chest:** *"hugging makes it way easier."* **Brace confirmed.**

His own summary: *"so elevated ankles and hugging makes these easier."*

**45/side milestone: *"i'm able to gently lay it on the support bars at 14 height; which i used to only be able to do without weight maybe a month back — was able to pause here at 3s and come up."*** The paused-squat prescription is doing exactly its job.

**80/side is a different problem and he named it precisely:** *"the equation definitely changes, i'm not able to go all the way down to 45 — partly it's thigh and brace strength mixed with anxiety, tho the support bars are there — the extra weight definitely makes this harder than just a stretching exercise."* Under load the limiter stops being mobility and becomes strength + brace + confidence.

**Set 2 > set 1, and he says it is a pattern:** *"second set this time and previously felt stronger and deeper — warmups help but strength somehow also gets better on second set; also deeper / feels more open too."*

**Set 3 is the floor-rising line of the block:** *"incredible depth at the third set, not as deep as 45 but felt pretty controlled; feels similar to what 45/s felt when we first started this program (which felt very hard at the beginning!)."*

sets.notes: Warmup round. Touched the pin-14 support bars, 3s pause, stood up.
Set 1 — shallowest. Load changes the limiter to thigh/brace strength plus anxiety.
Set 2 — "stronger and deeper," "more open." A repeated pattern, not a one-off.

**Station mismatch, and a useful one: the incline bench was occupied, so he ran a BARBELL RDL at 70/side.** *"Did regular rdl on 70 per side since someone was squatting the incline thing"* → confirmed on follow-up: *"that was 70/side with a bar."* ~185 total with the bar. **This is W29's planned hinge implement rotation arriving early by accident, and it is the sanctioned place for bar work** (the barbell is kept off pressing; the hinge is where it belongs).

**⚠️ GRIP FINDING: the left hand ran out and he flipped it to a mixed grip on the last set** — *"actually ran into left hand grip issues so i flipped my left hand last set."* Two things stack here: the flipped hand is supinated under load, which puts the left distal bicep tendon under tension at length — the exact tissue he described two days earlier on the incline curl (*"around tendon"*). And a mixed grip is the same class of workaround as straps, which he has ruled out on principle. **Recommendation given: stay double-overhand and let grip cap the load.**
